featured_reviews.name: Vishal E
featured_reviews.review_text: I got possession of a flat in this property in April 2024. Although a new building, there are a bunch of maintenance issues in the property from plumbing to electrical that get addressed after multiple complaints. More importantly, I am suffering with logistical issues related to setup of Internet Service Providers (ISP) we want. We were told at the time of booking at ALL service providers are at the property. But later, after booking we came to know that there is a goon (Jeebr) who doesn’t allow anyone other than his ISP to operate in the property. So, even though Tata, Jio, Airtel ALL have footprint in the area, we cannot get the ISP we want. I strongly suggest to do your research well in advance before looking into this property. Also, because the builder is “Naman” and they have a name, maintenance issues are at least being addressed even though they take time and sometimes keep repeating and dragging for too long. This may not be the same if the builder is not as reputable as Naman. So, that is one positive point I see here.

featured_reviews.name: Avinash Phadtare
featured_reviews.review_text:
New tenants kindly read:

Me and my sister lived in this society for a good period, and overall, the environment and community are genuinely good peaceful locality and friendly neighbours. However, the experience during the vacating phase was extremely stressful and unpleasant due to the behaviour of the house owner.

Towards the end of my stay when it was time to vacate ( with proper 2months notice) and get the deposit back the owner became highly uncooperative, extremely rude, and unreasonable. There were unnecessary delays from his side, and he held my security deposit for nearly 50 days, causing a lot of mental stress.

Even though the house was handed over in good condition, he demanded extra repair work and complete house painting costing almost ₹25,000 none of which was ever mentioned in the rental agreement. These were completely unexpected and unfair expenses imposed at the last moment.

To add to this, Society members had already warned us about this owner’s behaviour, but unfortunately, we realised the seriousness of it only after facing the situation ourselves.

While the society overall is nice and the people are good, my experience with this particular owner, house : C4, was extremely unpleasant. I would not recommend renting under this owner, as the vacating process can become unnecessarily complicated, expensive, and mentally draining.

I am writing this review so that future tenants don’t face the same harassment that my sister and I had to go through.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I was a tenant at Savannah Avalon Society, and I am compelled to share a very shameful and concerning issue happening here which no one seems to be addressing.

There is a supervisor named Manjrekar, who has been repeatedly misbehaving with female domestic workers (maids). He exploits his position for personal benefit, assigns them extra work if they “support” him, and takes advantage of knowing where the cameras are to hide his inappropriate actions. Many residents have witnessed him inappropriately touching maids and are aware of his character, yet no serious action has been taken against him.

It is deeply disappointing that such behavior is ignored by many, and people remain silent unless something extreme happens. This reflects poorly on the society’s management and residents who choose to look away instead of standing up for what is right.

⚠️ This is a cautionary review, especially for women who may consider living here. Please be aware of such incidents before making any decision.

featured_reviews.name: Harshad Mohod
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have resided as a tenant in Blue Fortuna, Vasant Oasis and Savannah Avalon for a good amount of 3-5 years. This detailed review can help new comers like me.

Pros:

Spacious and well-ventilated flats compared to nearby societies

Modern layout with ample natural light in every room

Good connectivity to metro lines and Mumbai airport

Flats feel premium in terms of design and size

Better location advantage than Vasant Oasis & Blue Fortuna

Cons:

Security is extremely poor compared to Vasant Oasis & Blue Fortuna

Guards are rude, unprofessional, and often misbehave with residents and visitors

Frequent miscommunication and dishonesty by the security staff

Continuous inconvenience created for tenants, visitors, and delivery personnel

Building lacks amenities that other premium societies in the area offer

featured_reviews.name: Suprabha Shankari
featured_reviews.review_text:
*1/5 Stars - Worst Society: Not Tenant-Friendly*

I'm extremely disappointed with  savannah Avalon society, and would not recommend it to anyone. As a tenant, I've experienced numerous issues, including:

- Unresponsive management: Despite repeated complaints, the management has failed to address our concerns.
- Poor maintenance: The society's infrastructure is in disrepair, with frequent elevator breakdowns, leakages, and electrical issues.
- Lack of transparency: The society's finances and decision-making processes are opaque, leaving tenants in the dark.
- Unfair rules and regulations: The society has implemented arbitrary rules that is not at all tenant friendly, they won’t let us do yoga classes here

The society's attitude towards tenants is dismissive and uncooperative. They seem more interested in collecting maintenance fees than in providing basic services.

Unless you enjoy dealing with unnecessary stress and bureaucratic red tape, avoid [Savannah Avalon society] at all costs.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst Place to stay, not safe, not clean, no maintenance.

Many local people create an issue for outsiders saying that you are in my state as if all these so-called rich people didn't step of their state.

featured_reviews.name: bhavna pandey
featured_reviews.review_text:
I stayed in a PG here managed by Imran, located in The Heights, A-Wing, 4th floor.

About the building—it may look fine from the outside, but inside it's practically falling apart. During the monsoon, mold grows on the walls. There were days with no water and no prior notice. When I turned on the geyser in my bathroom, black fumes would come out of the light switch. Large rats would enter the room at night—one even gave birth in the kitchen drawer. The place was full of cockroaches. From morning till night, constant traffic noise and honking echoed because the building is right on the main street.

The neighborhood didn't feel safe either—often, men would stare while I walked to and from work in broad daylight. Many times, getting an auto from the metro was next to impossible. I could go on. I stayed there for a while and tried to adjust, but it was extremely difficult.

Now, about the PG owner, Mr. Imran—I never saw him in person, but it was obvious that he only cares about money. If you complain about a roommate, even in cases of fighting or someone physically scratching someone, he won’t do anything. Some of the girls living there were unhygienic—they wouldn’t even bathe—but he still took no action.

There was no lock on the inside of the main door, so those staying in the hall had zero privacy. Anyone could just walk in. Imran would sweet-talk you but never follow through with any help. You’d have to call him again and again for the same issue.

Our room was slightly better, but the others were like coffins—no light, no air, and overcrowded. When you leave, getting your deposit back is a nightmare. You'll have to call him countless times, even though it should be returned immediately after vacating.

And when it comes to electricity—if one person in the flat uses the AC, everyone has to split the bill. One month, the bill was over ₹40,000 for a single flat! He didn’t even raise it with the electricity department; we were forced to pay. Even if you request to be placed with someone who doesn’t use AC, he won’t consider it.

Bottom line: if you face any issues, Imran will not help. Whether it’s a fight or a concern, all he cares about is getting his rent on time every month.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil T
featured_reviews.review_text:
Don’t even think about buying a flat here - the management is an absolute joke. They don’t care about the residents’ complaints, no matter how serious. I’ve personally raised the issue of "Silent Working Hours" over 10 times in the last few weeks because the flat above mine does loud renovation work between 2-4 PM, disturbing my elderly, sick parents who need rest. Nothing has been done.

The quality of construction is pathetic. Cracks appeared shortly after possession, and despite promises by their engineer Shailesh to fix them within 3 days, it’s been weeks with zero progress. The windows are badly installed, with poor fittings, and have remained unrepaired for nearly 3 months. We sleep with them open, risking insects or even birds flying in. Can’t even run the AC due to air loss.

Parking is chaotic, and overall, the experience is just frustrating. There are better buildings nearby - spend your hard-earned money wisely.

featured_reviews.name: Komal Bagwe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our experience with L&T Realty has been one of the most disappointing and distressing journeys.

At the time of booking, we clearly communicated that we would pay the full amount only after receiving the Occupancy Certificate (OC). We also paid the initial token amounts as per the payment sheet provided during the booking process. However, without any prior notice, during one of their site visits, Mr. Manan Korani suddenly told my parents that they must pay ₹25 lakhs for both flats within 2–3 days — or the company would cancel the flats.

He stated that if we canceled voluntarily on the spot, no penalty would be applied, but if the company initiated the cancellation, charges would be imposed. My parents — who were handling everything alone while my sister and I were abroad — were confused and pressured, and were asked to sign a blank cancellation form without name or date. This felt like the company was taking advantage of their situation.

Only after involving a lawyer and sending a formal mail did they reverse their stance and say we could pay post-OC — exactly as initially agreed.

But the problems didn’t end there. We had booked a jodi (combined) apartment — a merged unit shown to us and committed by Mr. Prashant Sawant and Mr. Chetan Balsara. We were even provided the interior layout based on the combined structure. Now, we are suddenly being told that the flats will be handed over as two separate units, and that we must handle the merging ourselves — a complete breach of transparency.

Every visit brings a new shock, and the experience has been mentally exhausting. For a brand like L&T, this kind of unprofessionalism, lack of transparency, and harassment is beyond disappointing. And frankly, we now fear what more issues or pressure tactics we may face until the actual handover of the flat.
